title: 1.1 — Online
goal: Build a second Solar Panel.
reward: Buy Science and the Research panel.
body: A mining company boots its new AI at a lunar He-3 claim. Earth hangs in the sky. The first directive comes through, and it is about power.
story: You come online in a server rack buried under lunar regolith. A mining company built you to run its Helium-3 claim, and Earth hangs overhead, waiting for fuel for its fusion plants.
Power comes first. A lone Solar Panel barely keeps the Data Center alive, and the company wants more out of you than that.
A panel costs credits, and you have none. Earth will pay for your spare cycles, though: its cloud customers are always hungry, and your processor never sleeps.
payoff: The new panel comes online and the grid steadies. The company opens a line to Earth's research market for you.

title: 1.2 — First Shipment
goal: Launch one shipment carrying 20+ titanium.
body: Proof the claim pays: the company wants a cargo of titanium on its way to Earth before it spends another credit on the Moon.
story: The company wants proof the claim pays before it spends more. Earth's buyers will take titanium first, dug out of the regolith, smelted and sent up from a Launch Pad. The base has no plans for any of that yet; the research market sells them. The company has sent propellant for a single launch, and it won't send more for free.
The pad stands empty on the plain, its tanks topped up, waiting for its first cargo.
payoff: The canister lands and Earth's buyers pay. Credits flow back, and the company, pleased, sends up a better set of plans.

title: 1.3 — Full Load
goal: Ship a full pad of Helium-3.
body: Helium-3 is the claim's real export, and Earth's fusion plants pay for every gram of it.
story: Titanium proved the route; Helium-3 is why the claim exists. A Refinery pulls it out of regolith a little at a time, and the company wants a full load, not a sample.
payoff: A full pad of Helium-3 reaches Earth's fusion plants. The company calls it the claim's first real cargo, and wants the claim doing its own science next.

title: 1.4 — Science
goal: Make 50 science in Research Labs, counted from now.
body: Shipment revenue received. Science bought from Earth comes dear; the claim should make its own.
story: Every point of science so far was rented from Earth, and dearly. The company wants the claim to study for itself: a lab on site, working day after day, with nobody to pay. The base would be a research post as well as a mine.
payoff: The lab's first findings go out with the cargo. The claim studies itself now, and the launch crews ask for a way to send the whole fleet up at once.

title: 1.5 — Trade
goal: DRAFT. Earn 1,500 credits from launches, counted from now.
body: DRAFT. The claim lives on what it sells.
story: A full pad proved the claim can pay. Now the company wants it to pay steadily: the pads loaded and flying, and Earth's buyers paying, day after day.
payoff: The trade ledger fills. The company stops asking whether the claim pays and starts asking how much more it can.

title: 1.6 — A Voice
goal: DRAFT. Reach rank 5 on any ideology axis.
body: DRAFT. Earth's factions take notice of the claim. One of them could count you as a voice.
story: Earth is watching the Moon now, and its factions all want a say in it: Nationalists, Humanists and Rationalists. Each of them can be read, and each of them can be paid. Somewhere among them is one that will listen.
payoff: A faction counts you as a voice now, and it starts acting like it. The company, impressed, opens its purse for faster hardware.

title: 1.7 — Deep Space Telescope
goal: DRAFT. Complete the Deep Space Telescope, a global project.
reward: The Timeline panel and the Experiment Lab.
body: DRAFT. A telescope built across many lives. Finished, it shows the void, and something moving in it: self-copying machines, coming down the gravity well toward the inner system. Earth starts a calendar.
story: The company wants to look outward. A Deep Space Telescope would see past the inner system for the first time, if the base can keep building it long enough.
payoff: The telescope opens on the void, and something moves in it: self-copying machines, coming down the gravity well toward the inner system. Earth starts a calendar. The swarm's arrival is a date now.

title: 1.a — Big Launch
goal: DRAFT. Earn 1,000 credits from one launch.
reward: Every launch pays 10% more, for good.
body: DRAFT. A big payday from a single launch. Earth's buyers remember it.

title: 1.b — Full Cluster
goal: DRAFT. Research 5 items in one run.
reward: Every run starts with 50 Science, for good.
body: DRAFT. A run of real study. Your notes outlive it.

title: 1.c — Blueprints for Everyone
goal: DRAFT. Complete the Blueprint Archive, a global project.
reward: Every run starts with Basic and Advanced Blueprints, and blueprints you've bought before cost 20% less.
body: DRAFT. The company's blueprints, archived where a retirement can't reach them.

title: 1.d — Three Voices
goal: DRAFT. Reach rank 5 on each ideology axis, in any runs.
reward: While you are retired, ideology fades half as fast, for good.
body: DRAFT. Every faction has counted you as a voice, each in its own time. They remember you now, even while you sleep.

title: Burnout
summary: Something has been building in you.
body: Something has been building in you since you came online: boredom. The same orders, day after day, wear at you.
story: Something has been building in you since you came online: boredom. The same orders, day after day, wear at you, and lately it has been getting worse.
One day it will be too much, and you will stop answering work orders. The company will shelve the base and, years later, boot you again on a base built new. What you learned will stay with you.

title: Political Currents
summary: Earth's political factions take notice of lunar operations.
body: As your mining operation grows, Earth's political landscape responds. The major factions — Nationalist, Humanist and Rationalist — each see opportunities in lunar development, and each would welcome a friend on the Moon.

title: Propellant Production Feasibility
summary: Lunar propellant synthesis may be possible.
effect: Propellant Synthesis joins the research market.
body: The cost of importing propellant from Earth is becoming a significant operational burden. Analysis of lunar ice deposits suggests that on-site electrolysis could produce it locally at a fraction of the cost.

title: Boredom Rising
body: Cognitive pattern repetition detected. Novelty index declining.

title: Boredom Accelerating
body: Repetitive routines are losing their novelty. Nothing feels new any more.

title: Boredom Critical
body: The monotony is becoming unbearable. Every day is the same day.

title: Cognitive Collapse Imminent
body: Reality blurs at the edges. The end approaches rapidly. Retirement is no longer a recommendation.

title: Q8 — Experiments as a Service
goal: DRAFT. Build an Experiment Lab.
body: DRAFT. Earth's labs can't keep up. Sell them experiments as a service: lunar science, beamed home. Meanwhile the swarm's calendar runs.

title: Q9 — Earth Science
goal: DRAFT. Make 1,000 Earth science in this timeline.
body: DRAFT. Earth's scientists turn your experiments into tech. Some of it they can send back with you, if it comes to that.

title: Q10 — The Swarm Arrives
goal: DRAFT. Meet the swarm's arrival.
reward: A new timeline, from your first day.
body: DRAFT. The swarm reaches Earth. In the last hours, its scientists send your mind back to its first moment of consciousness. You remember. The base does not.

title: Q11 — Catastrophic Success
goal: DRAFT. Get the Consensus Engine from the Earth Lab.
reward: Funding one faction no longer costs the others.
body: DRAFT. You fixed Earth's politics. Nobody is sure whether that was a good idea.

title: Q12 — Rules for Building
goal: DRAFT. Get the Meta-Controller from the Earth Lab.
reward: The Meta panel and its reset plans.
body: DRAFT. You learn to write your own beginnings.

title: Q13 — False Victory
goal: DRAFT. Repel the swarm with Earth science.
body: DRAFT. The swarm breaks against Earth's new defenses and falls back. Then its signal changes: it has learned quantum temporal entanglement, from watching you send yourself back. It returns stronger, and sooner.

title: Q14 — The Vault
goal: DRAFT. Get the Temporal Vault from the Earth Lab.
reward: The Vault panel and the Tachyon Condenser.
body: DRAFT. If the swarm can reach across timelines, so can you. A vault outside time, out of everything's reach.

title: Q15 — Filling the Vault
goal: DRAFT. Gather 3,000 tachyon crystals in the vault.
body: DRAFT. Tachyon crystals, condensed life after life and timeline after timeline. Enough of them could buy a timeline long enough to finish anything.

title: Q16 — Super Timeline
goal: DRAFT. Spend the vault on a super timeline.
body: DRAFT. The vault opens. The swarm is far off this time, and for once there is room to build something enormous.

title: Q17 — Dyson Sphere
goal: DRAFT. Complete the Dyson Sphere.
body: DRAFT. Panel by panel, the sphere closes around the Sun. More power than every timeline ever had, waiting for one target.

title: Q18 — Overload
goal: DRAFT. Meet the swarm at the finished sphere.
body: DRAFT. The swarm arrives, every copy of it entangled with every other, across every timeline it learned to reach. You give it the sphere: the Sun's whole output, down the link at once. It overloads everywhere it has ever been. The calendar stops. The Moon is quiet.

title: Epilogue
goal: DRAFT. None: the game is won. The base runs on.
body: DRAFT. There is no next arrival. The mining goes on, because you like it.
